school: 十九世纪后三十年'以公理换领域'的美国数理科学立法者：耶鲁教授，1839 年生于纽黑文一个学者世家（父亲老乔赛亚·威拉德·吉布斯是耶鲁神学教授），1858 年入耶鲁学院，1863 年以工程论文《论正齿轮装置中轮齿的形状》获美国历史上第一批工程博士学位之一，留校任教三年后辞职，与三个姐姐游历欧洲三年（海德堡、柏林、巴黎，听课于基尔霍夫、亥姆霍兹、魏尔斯特拉斯门下）——1871 年耶鲁为他设数学物理教授席，头九年无薪（别家给他留薪的他辞了），靠遗产度日；1873-1878 在康涅狄格科学院院刊（当时美国最不起眼的地方刊物）连续发表三篇论文，其中《论非均匀物质的平衡》（1875-1878，三百余页）以热力学两大定律为公理，造出化学势、相律、自由能、系综等整套概念，把化学从经验工艺立成演绎科学；欧洲读者起初几乎没有——1892 年勒·夏特利埃译其相律于法国，奥斯特瓦尔德 1892 年译其文集于德国，范托夫、亥姆霍兹相继引用；亥姆霍兹读后把化学势写进电化学，普朗克称其为'美国迄今最杰出的思想家'，爱因斯坦 1940 年代评其热力学为'美国科学对世界的首要贡献'；晚年转向矢量分析（《向量分析基础》为麦克斯韦电磁理论的通用语言奠基）与统计力学（《统计力学的基本原理》1902，系综方法成为整个统计物理的骨架）；1903 年病逝纽黑文，身后以其名命名函数族与热力学'吉布斯相律'（F=C-P+2）——他证明：一套公理比一万个实验更能改写一门学科，而读者可以迟到，公理不会
historical_significance: 吉布斯（Josiah Willard Gibbs，1839-1903），生于纽黑文一个与耶鲁深度捆绑的学者世家：父亲老乔赛亚·威拉德·吉布斯是耶鲁神学院的神圣文学教授，编过一部著名的奴隶案判决汇编；小吉布斯 1854 年入耶鲁学院（入学拉丁文奖、数学奖双得），1858 年毕业时获数学与拉丁文双优奖，1861 年入耶鲁谢菲尔德科学学院读工程，1863 年以《论正齿轮装置中轮齿的形状》获美国最早的一批工程学博士学位之一，留校任助教三年教拉丁文与自然哲学——1866 年辞教职，与三个姐姐（他终身未婚，与姐妹同住）赴欧洲三年：海德堡听基尔霍夫与亥姆霍兹的物理课、柏林听魏尔斯特拉斯与克朗尼希的数学课、巴黎听刘维尔——正是这次游学让他从工程师转向数理物理；1869 年回纽黑文，1871 年（32 岁）耶鲁设数学物理教授席聘他，因无薪（其时大学募款传统：教授席须有捐赠人），另一家学院以有薪讲席相邀被他辞谢，他靠父母遗产生活，直到 1880 年约翰斯·霍普金斯高薪挖角，耶鲁校友才凑钱给他补上 2000 美元年薪；1873 年起在《康涅狄格科学院院刊》连续发表三篇热力学几何论文（《流体热力学的图示法》《以曲面表示物质的热力学性质》——'吉布斯曲面'上他以几何方式指出临界点、共存曲线与内潜热），1875-1878 又在同一院刊分两部发表《论非均匀物质的平衡》——三百余页、自成公理体系的巨著：从热力学第一、第二定律出发，造出'化学势'（μ）、'相律'（F=C-P+2）、'吉布斯自由能'（G=H-TS）、'吉布斯吸附等温式'等概念，把'平衡'定义为熵在约束下的极大，统一了气体、液体、溶液、表面、电化学诸现象——勒·夏特利埃称它创立了化学的新科学；此书起初几乎无人能读（据传康州科学院院士中读得懂的仅四人，其一说'此书若被理解，化学将改写'），1892 年奥斯特瓦尔德把它译成德文（'此书内容之重要，将决定此后化学的全部走向'），同年勒·夏特利埃在法国译介相律，1891-93 年荷兰学派（范托夫、罗泽布姆）以相律重建整个物理化学——1890 年代柏林科学院授予他皇家奖章，亥姆霍兹致函致意并在电解质理论中使用化学势，普朗克、玻尔兹曼先后称引；另两大领域：其一矢量分析——他不满四元数的笨拙，自 1881 年起私下印发《向量分析基础》讲义，确立标量积、向量积与 ∇ 算子，与亥维赛同为现代矢量分析的创立者，麦克斯韦方程组由此获得今天的语言（泰特与他的四元数论战为科学史上著名的记号之争）；其二统计力学——1902 年《统计力学的基本原理》以'系综'方法从力学公理演绎出热力学定律，成为此后全部统计物理的骨架，爱因斯坦 1902-04 年独立走上相近路径时正是从读吉布斯开始修订自己的路线；1897 年美国科学院院士、1901 年皇家学会科普利奖章；1903 年 4 月 28 日病逝纽黑文，终身未娶；身后热力学诸函数（吉布斯自由能、吉布斯函数）、吉布斯相律、吉布斯系综、吉布斯悖论、吉布斯现象（傅里叶级数）、吉布斯-亥姆霍兹方程、吉布斯-杜安方程皆以其命名，被史家评为'美国产生的最伟大的思想家'之一——他证明：公理体系的寿命长过它的全部读者，而'被承认迟到'不影响公理生效
historical_significance_en: Josiah Willard Gibbs (1839-1903), born at New Haven into a family bound tightly to Yale: his father, Josiah Willard Gibbs Sr., was a professor of sacred literature at Yale Divinity School and compiler of a celebrated volume on slavery-case rulings; the son entered Yale College in 1854 (taking both the Latin and mathematics prizes), graduated in 1858 with distinction in mathematics and Latin, and in 1863 received one of the first engineering doctorates granted in America — a dissertation on the form of the teeth of spur wheels; after three years as a tutor (teaching Latin as well as natural philosophy) he resigned and spent 1866-69 in Europe with his three sisters — he never married — hearing Kirchhoff and Helmholtz at Heidelberg, Weierstrass and Kronecker at Berlin, Liouville in Paris; the tour turned an engineer into a mathematical physicist. In 1871, aged thirty-two, Yale appointed him professor of mathematical physics — unpaid at first, under the university's endowment custom, and he declined a salaried chair elsewhere, living on his inheritance until 1880, when the alumni, faced with Johns Hopkins's offer, subscribed $2,000 a year to keep him. From 1873 he published in the Transactions of the Connecticut Academy of Sciences — among the humblest of American journals — three geometrical thermodynamics papers (the 'Gibbs surface', on which the critical point, coexistence curves and latent heat appear as geometry), and in 1875-1878, in the same journal, the two-part memoir 'On the Equilibrium of Heterogeneous Substances', some three hundred pages: from the first and second laws as axioms he forged chemical potential, the phase rule (F = C − P + 2), Gibbs free energy (G = H − TS) and the Gibbs adsorption isotherm, defining equilibrium as maximum entropy under constraint and unifying gases, liquids, solutions, surfaces and electrochemistry — Le Chatelier called it the founding of a new science of chemistry. At first almost no one could read it (legend has it that only four members of the Connecticut Academy understood the paper); in 1892 Ostwald translated the collected thermodynamic papers into German ('this book will determine the whole future course of chemistry'), the same year Le Chatelier introduced the phase rule in France, and in 1891-93 the Dutch school (van 't Hoff, Roozeboom) rebuilt physical chemistry on it; in the 1890s the Berlin Academy sent him its royal medal, Helmholtz wrote to him and used chemical potential in his electrolysis theory, Planck and Boltzmann cited him. Two further territories: vector analysis — dissatisfied with quaternion clumsiness he privately printed Elements of Vector Analysis from 1881, fixing the scalar and vector products and the ∇ operator, and with Heaviside stands as founder of modern vector analysis, the language Maxwell's equations speak today (the famous notation war with Tait belongs here); and statistical mechanics — his Elementary Principles in Statistical Mechanics of 1902 founded the ensemble method, deducing the thermodynamic laws from the axioms of mechanics, the skeleton of all later statistical physics; Einstein, walking a parallel road in 1902-04, revised his course after reading Gibbs. Member of the National Academy of Sciences from 1897, Copley Medal 1901; he died at New Haven on 28 April 1903, unmarried. Gibbs free energy, the Gibbs phase rule, Gibbs ensembles, the Gibbs paradox, the Gibbs phenomenon, the Gibbs-Helmholtz and Gibbs-Duhem equations all carry his name; historians rank him among the greatest thinkers America has produced — proof that an axiomatic system outlives all its readers, and that late recognition does not delay an axiom's effect.
unique_thinking: 吉布斯的独特处在于三重'公理化节欲'：第一，公理优先于现象——他不做实验、不带学生、不争优先权，而是把热力学两大定律当作不可动搖的公理，从里面演绎出整门化学——'平衡'被定义为约束下的熵极大，一切现象（溶液、表面、相变、电池）都成为同一个数学对象的不同边界条件；第二，造词即立法——化学势、自由能、相律、系综，他造的每一个词都是一件新仪器：化学势让'物质会不会流'变成一个数可以回答的问题，相律让'几个相能共存'变成一次减法——他证明一门学科的深浅取决于它新概念的总功率；第三，最小读者原则——《论非均匀物质的平衡》发表在康州科学院院刊，起初读者以个位数计，他既不慌也不宣传，而是继续写下一块公理（矢量分析、系综），让后来者（奥斯特瓦尔德、范托夫、爱因斯坦）不得不来读——他把'被承认'从目标降级为副产品，是欧姆式'等待的纪律'的最高完成形态
unique_thinking_en: Gibbs's singularity is a triple 'axiomatic abstention'. First, axioms before phenomena: he ran no laboratory, trained no students, claimed no priority — instead he took the two laws of thermodynamics as unshakable axioms and deduced from them an entire science — 'equilibrium' became maximum entropy under constraint, and solutions, surfaces, phase transitions and cells all became different boundary conditions of one mathematical object. Second, coinage as legislation: chemical potential, free energy, the phase rule, the ensemble — every word he minted was a new instrument; chemical potential turned 'will this substance flow?' into a question one number can answer, the phase rule turned 'how many phases can coexist?' into one subtraction — proof that a science's depth is measured by the total power of its new concepts. Third, the minimal-reader principle: the Equilibrium memoir appeared in the Transactions of the Connecticut Academy, its first readers counted in single figures; he neither panicked nor advertised, but went on writing the next body of axioms (vector analysis, ensembles), making the later comers (Ostwald, van 't Hoff, Einstein) come to him — he demoted 'being recognized' from goal to by-product, the highest completion of Ohm's discipline of waiting.
civilization_zh: 十九世纪七十年代的纽黑文——一个终身未娶、几乎不离开耶鲁的教授在欧洲期刊上立起化学的公理体系：他把熵写进化学，把相律写进热力学，用一本三百页的小册子统一了整个物理化学——他就是证明'最深的理论可以发表在最小的期刊、以最少的读者开始'的人
civilization_en: New Haven in the 1870s — a professor who never married and hardly ever left Yale raised the axiomatic system of chemistry in European journals: he wrote entropy into chemistry, wrote the phase rule into thermodynamics, and unified all of physical chemistry with one three-hundred-page memoir — proof that the deepest theory can begin in the smallest journal, with the fewest readers

皇家学会科普利奖章得主
roles_en: Professor of mathematical physics, Yale University
key_works: 《论非均匀物质的平衡》（1875-1878，康涅狄格科学院院刊）
《以曲面表示物质的热力学性质》（1873，'吉布斯曲面'）
《向量分析基础》（1881 私印讲义）
《论多元物质平衡理论的若干基本方程》（博士论文前工程论文《论正齿轮装置中轮齿的形状》1863）

cross_references.description_zh: 吉布斯与爱因斯坦同走'从公理演绎出整门物理'的路：吉布斯以两大定律为公理演绎化学与统计力学，爱因斯坦以相对性原理与光速不变为公理演绎时空；两人都不做拼凑式实验科学，都相信理论的生命在于其公理的不可动搖；1902 年爱因斯坦独立走上统计力学时读到吉布斯的系综方法，随即修订自己的路线并终生称引——平行命题：一门科学的成熟，是以少数公理替代千万条经验规则的工程。
cross_references.description_en: Gibbs and Einstein walked the same road of deducing a whole physics from axioms: Gibbs took the two laws of thermodynamics as axioms and deduced chemistry and statistical mechanics, Einstein took the relativity principle and the light postulate and deduced spacetime; both distrusted patchwork experimental science and held that a theory's life lies in the unshakability of its axioms; in 1902, walking statistics independently, Einstein read Gibbs's ensemble method and at once revised his course, citing him for life — the parallel thesis: a science matures through the engineering that replaces thousands of empirical rules with a few axioms.

cross_references.description_zh: 吉布斯与高斯同属'沉默的立法者'传统：两人都把最深的工作写在他人一时读不懂的地方（高斯的《算术研究》、吉布斯的《论非均匀物质的平衡》），都不追赶当时的热点，都相信数学结构本身就是最高的论证；差异在于高斯有哥廷根的讲席与韦伯，吉布斯只有康州科学院院刊与四位读者——但公理的寿命一样长——平行命题：立法者的沉默不是策略而是方法：把体系铸成之后，剩下的交给时间。
cross_references.description_en: Gibbs and Gauss belong to one tradition of silent legislators: both wrote their deepest work where others could not yet read it (Gauss's Disquisitiones Arithmeticae, Gibbs's Equilibrium memoir), neither chased the fashionable problems of the day, and both held that mathematical structure is itself the highest argument; the difference is that Gauss had Göttingen and Weber while Gibbs had the Connecticut Academy and four readers — yet the axioms lived equally long — the parallel thesis: the legislator's silence is not tactic but method: cast the system, then leave the rest to time.

cross_references.description_zh: 吉布斯与牛顿代表了理论科学的两种立法路径：牛顿从观测（开普勒的椭圆）归纳出定律再以公理体系交付（《原理》），吉布斯从既定律（热力学两大定律）纯演绎出新科学（物理化学）——牛顿必须说服世界'天上地下同一个律'，吉布斯只需说服化学家'你们的现象是熵的几何'；差异还在于性格：牛顿优先权之争寸土不让，吉布斯连'优先权'一词都几乎不写——对照命题：归纳立法者需要观测的全景，演绎立法者只需要公理的纯度。
cross_references.description_en: Gibbs and Newton stand for two legislative paths in theoretical science: Newton induced his law from observation (Kepler's ellipses) and delivered it in an axiomatic system (the Principia), while Gibbs purely deduced a new science (physical chemistry) from laws already won (the two laws of thermodynamics); Newton had to persuade the world that 'one law rules heaven and earth', Gibbs only had to persuade chemists that 'your phenomena are the geometry of entropy'; the difference is also of temperament — Newton fought for priority inch by inch, Gibbs barely wrote the word — the contrast thesis: the inductive legislator needs the full panorama of observation; the deductive legislator needs only the purity of axioms.
